statement: Picture 1 is a square with a star in its top left corner and 1 dot. Each new picture moves the star one corner clockwise and adds a dot. What does picture 10 look like?

choices.text: The star is in the top right corner, with 9 dots
choices.misconception: I counted only the 9 dots added after picture 1 and forgot the dot that picture 1 already has.

choices.text: The star is in the top right corner, with 10 dots
The star is in the top right corner, with 11 dots
choices.misconception: I added 10 new dots to picture 1, but from picture 1 to picture 10 there are only 9 new pictures.

choices.text: The star is in the bottom right corner, with 10 dots
choices.misconception: I moved the star 10 times, but from picture 1 to picture 10 it only moves 9 times.

choices.text: The star is in the bottom left corner, with 10 dots
choices.misconception: I moved the star anticlockwise instead of clockwise.

hints: The star and the dots change separately. Follow each one on its own.
The star goes round 4 corners, so its place repeats every 4 pictures. The dots simply go up by 1 each time. Count how many moves there are from picture 1 to picture 10.
From picture 1 to picture 10 there are 9 moves, which is 2 full trips round the square and 1 more corner. Picture 1 has 1 dot and picture 2 has 2 dots, so picture 10 has 10 dots.

solutions.reliable: The star: it is in the top left corner in pictures 1, 5 and 9, because every 4 moves bring it back. Picture 10 is one move after picture 9, so the star is in the top right corner. The dots: picture 1 has 1 dot, picture 2 has 2 dots, and so on, so picture 10 has 10 dots. Picture 10 has the star in the top right corner and 10 dots. The transferable idea: when a pattern changes two things at once, follow each change on its own and then put them together.
solutions.elegant: The star is in the top right corner in pictures 2, 6, 10, and so on, every 4 pictures starting from picture 2. Every picture has as many dots as its number. So picture 10: top right, 10 dots.

whyOnTest: A pattern that changes two things at once, one going round a cycle and one that keeps growing, is a common Kangaroo trap.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
